content.user_title: Add User Approval to Caffeine AI Apps
content.value_statement: Applications need a controlled way to admit users before exposing protected features. This skill guides backend approval checks and frontend administration workflows.
actual_capabilities: Integrates Caffeine AI authorization and user approval modules into a Motoko actor.
Defines functions for approval status checks, requests, decisions, and approval lists.
Restricts approval decisions and user listings to administrators.
Outlines a frontend flow for pending, approved, rejected, and administrator states.
Specifies an administrator dashboard for approval decisions and role management.
limitations: Requires the separate authorization extension and compatible Caffeine AI packages.
Uses a prefabricated approval module that the application cannot modify.
Provides integration guidance and examples, not a complete deployed application.
Developers must add and test approval checks on every protected public function.

use_cases.title: Protect Motoko Features
use_cases.description: Add approval checks and administrator controls to protected backend functions.

use_cases.title: Build an Approval Experience
use_cases.description: Create request, status, blocked-access, and administrator views for application users.

use_cases.title: Manage Application Access
use_cases.description: Review pending users, approve or reject requests, and coordinate role assignments.

prompt_templates.title: Add the Basic Approval Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Add this user approval extension to my Caffeine AI app. Show the required backend functions and explain where approval checks belong.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner integration into a new application

prompt_templates.title: Design Approval Screens
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the frontend states for pending, approved, rejected, and administrator users. Include request actions, status messages, and blocked feature behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Admin Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an administrator workflow that lists users, changes approval status, and manages roles. Keep all privileged actions restricted to administrators.

prompt_templates.title: Audit End-to-End Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backend and frontend approval implementation. Identify public functions without approval checks, unsafe administrator actions, and inconsistent user states.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review of an existing application

output_examples.input: Add approval checks to my protected profile and billing features.
output: Administrators retain access to both features.
Approved users can access profile and billing functions.
Pending and rejected users receive a clear authorization error.

output_examples.input: Plan the user approval screen for a pending user.
output_examples.output: The screen shows pending status, disables protected navigation, and provides one approval request action with clear progress feedback.
The dashboard lists each user and status, supports approve or reject decisions, and keeps role assignment behind administrator authorization.

best_practices: Apply authorization and approval checks inside every protected backend function.
Treat backend checks as authoritative even when the frontend hides restricted features.
Test pending, approved, rejected, and administrator users across every protected workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on frontend visibility to enforce access.
Do not expose approval decisions or user listings to non-administrators.
Do not assume new public functions inherit approval checks automatically.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It adds guidance for approval requests, approval decisions, status checks, protected features, and administrator management.

faq.question: Does this replace role-based authorization?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the authorization extension and combines roles with approval status.

faq.question: Are administrators required to request approval?
faq.answer: No. The documented initialization automatically approves existing administrators, and administrator checks allow access.

faq.question: Can users approve themselves?
faq.answer: No. Users can request approval, but only administrators should change approval status.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a finished interface?
faq.answer: No. It defines expected frontend behavior and backend interfaces for developers to implement.

faq.question: Where must approval checks be added?
faq.answer: Add them inside every public backend function that should serve only approved users or administrators.
